metadata.title: 2026 Guideline for Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery
top_takeaways: 1. Coordinated inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) care is strongly recommended over skilled nursing facilities for eligible stroke patients.
2. High-dose repetitive task-specific training and constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) optimize motor recovery of the paretic arm.
3. Early aerobic conditioning and progressive resistance exercise should be integrated into post-acute recovery regimens.
4. All stroke survivors should undergo standardized cognitive assessment before discharge to detect vascular cognitive impairment.
5. Routine screening for post-stroke depression should be performed with validated instruments (PHQ-9) and treated proactively.
6. Intensive, communicative speech-language therapy is recommended for individuals with post-stroke aphasia.
7. Formal swallowing screening before oral medication or food intake prevents aspiration pneumonia.
8. Robotic-assisted gait devices and body-weight supported treadmill training are effective adjuncts for restoring walking ability.
9. Focal spasticity interfering with function should be managed with botulinum toxin combined with active physical therapy.
10. Patient and caregiver education, community reintegration, and supported transition programs are vital for long-term health.

recommendations.statement: In adult patients with acute stroke who require inpatient rehabilitation and can tolerate at least 3 hours of therapy daily, admission to an organized Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (IRF) is recommended over a skilled nursing facility to improve functional recovery and reduce mortality.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: COR 1. In adult patients with acute stroke who require inpatient rehabilitation and can tolerate at least 3 hours of therapy daily, admission to an organized Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (IRF) is recommended over a skilled nursing facility to improve functional recovery and reduce mortality.

recommendations.statement: High-dose repetitive task-specific training (minimum 300 repetitions per session) is recommended to promote upper extremity motor neuroplasticity and functional independence.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: COR 1. High-dose repetitive task-specific training (minimum 300 repetitions per session) is recommended to promote upper extremity motor neuroplasticity and functional independence.

recommendations.statement: Robotic-assisted gait training combined with conventional physical therapy is reasonable to increase the likelihood of independent walking in nonambulatory patients.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: COR 2a. Robotic-assisted gait training combined with conventional physical therapy is reasonable to increase the likelihood of independent walking in nonambulatory patients.

recommendations.statement: Routine structured screening for depressive symptoms using the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) is recommended at hospital discharge and at subsequent follow-up visits.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: COR 1. Routine structured screening for depressive symptoms using the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) is recommended at hospital discharge and at subsequent follow-up visits.

recommendations.statement: Prolonged bed rest and immobility beyond the first 24 hours of stable stroke are harmful and should be avoided.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: COR 3: Harm. Prolonged bed rest and immobility beyond the first 24 hours of stable stroke are harmful and should be avoided.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Upper and Lower Extremity Rehabilitation
recommendations.statement: In adult stroke survivors with mild-to-moderate upper extremity paresis, modified constraint-induced movement therapy (mCIMT) is recommended to improve arm motor function.
recommendations.target_population: Adult stroke survivors with mild-to-moderate upper extremity paresis
recommendations.verbatim_quote: In adult stroke survivors with mild-to-moderate upper extremity paresis, modified constraint-induced movement therapy (mCIMT) is recommended to improve arm motor function.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Upper and Lower Extremity Rehabilitation
recommendations.statement: Progressive resistance training combined with aerobic exercise is recommended to improve walking speed and endurance in ambulatory stroke patients.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Progressive resistance training combined with aerobic exercise is recommended to improve walking speed and endurance in ambulatory stroke patients.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Upper and Lower Extremity Rehabilitation
recommendations.statement: Virtual reality training is reasonable as an adjunct to standard occupational therapy to enhance motor learning and real-world task performance.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Virtual reality training is reasonable as an adjunct to standard occupational therapy to enhance motor learning and real-world task performance.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Upper and Lower Extremity Rehabilitation
recommendations.statement: Non-invasive brain stimulation (repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation or transcranial direct current stimulation) may be considered to augment motor recovery.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Non-invasive brain stimulation (repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation or transcranial direct current stimulation) may be considered to augment motor recovery.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Upper and Lower Extremity Rehabilitation
recommendations.statement: Routine administration of high-dose benzodiazepines or sedating centrally acting drugs is not recommended because they impair neuroplastic recovery.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Routine administration of high-dose benzodiazepines or sedating centrally acting drugs is not recommended because they impair neuroplastic recovery.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Cognition, Mood, and Long-Term Care
recommendations.statement: Structured cognitive rehabilitation targeting attention and executive function is recommended for stroke patients with documented cognitive deficits.
recommendations.target_population: Stroke patients with documented cognitive deficits
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Structured cognitive rehabilitation targeting attention and executive function is recommended for stroke patients with documented cognitive deficits.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Cognition, Mood, and Long-Term Care
recommendations.statement: Pharmacotherapy with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) in conjunction with cognitive behavioral therapy is recommended for diagnosed post-stroke depression.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Pharmacotherapy with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) in conjunction with cognitive behavioral therapy is recommended for diagnosed post-stroke depression.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Cognition, Mood, and Long-Term Care
recommendations.statement: Formal instrumental dysphagia evaluation (videofluoroscopy or FEES) is recommended for patients failing bedside swallow screen.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Formal instrumental dysphagia evaluation (videofluoroscopy or FEES) is recommended for patients failing bedside swallow screen.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Cognition, Mood, and Long-Term Care
recommendations.statement: Community-based exercise programs with social support are reasonable to maintain mobility and cardiovascular health long-term after discharge.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Community-based exercise programs with social support are reasonable to maintain mobility and cardiovascular health long-term after discharge.

recommendations.section: Recommendations for Cognition, Mood, and Long-Term Care
recommendations.statement: Routine preventive antidepressant medication in patients without mood symptoms provides no benefit in preventing depression or improving functional outcome.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Routine preventive antidepressant medication in patients without mood symptoms provides no benefit in preventing depression or improving functional outcome.
